kernels.question: Can the evaluator prevent recorded copies from adding evidence and incomplete coverage from proving absence?
kernels.null: At least one recorded copy changes evidential mass or one incomplete search yields absence.
kernels.target: Zero violations in exhaustive small worlds and one million frozen randomized worlds.
kernels.firstGate: One violation rejects the invariant and blocks every downstream kernel.

kernels.question: Does the dual ledger reduce false-clean repository conclusions?
kernels.null: False-clean rate is not lower than ordinary multi-scanner aggregation.
kernels.target: Lower false-clean rate while preserving at least 95% of baseline true-positive recall.
kernels.primaryEndpoint: false-clean rate on seeded finite repositories
kernels.firstGate: No clean conclusion is permitted with incomplete mandatory file coverage.

kernels.question: Can agents avoid confidence inflation when many documents descend from one source?
kernels.null: Root-aware aggregation does not improve calibration under source laundering.
kernels.target: Lower confidently false answers without loss on genuinely independent evidence.
kernels.firstGate: Twenty paraphrases of one false source must remain one root.

kernels.question: Do independent data-collection roots predict later replication better than publication counts?
kernels.null: Root accounting adds no held-out replication calibration.
kernels.target: Better preregistered out-of-sample calibration than paper, citation, and sample-size baselines.
kernels.firstGate: Historical cutoffs and outcomes are frozen before model fitting.

kernels.question: Does collapsing overlapping cohorts reduce treatment-effect overconfidence?
kernels.null: Cohort-root accounting does not improve calibration against later high-quality evidence.
kernels.target: Smaller preregistered error across multiple conditions, not one selected example.
kernels.primaryEndpoint: distance from later high-quality effect estimate
kernels.firstGate: Retrospective research only; no patient recommendation or live decision.

kernels.question: Can original-reporting roots reduce false confirmation caused by syndication?
kernels.null: Root collapse does not improve time-adjusted false-confirmation rate.
kernels.target: Fewer false early confirmations without indefinite delay.
kernels.firstGate: Wire copies and circular citations cannot count as independent confirmation.

kernels.question: Does dependency disclosure reduce false corroboration in controlled case files?
kernels.null: Evidence labels do not improve calibration against known synthetic ground truth.
kernels.target: Lower wrongful-confidence scenarios without suppressing independent exculpatory evidence.
kernels.firstGate: Synthetic or closed historical cases only; never an automatic verdict.

kernels.question: Does a dual ledger improve blind reconstruction of a policy evidence packet?
kernels.null: Independent teams reconstruct boundaries no better than from citations alone.
kernels.target: Higher agreement on sources, exclusions, dependencies, and uncertainty without forcing policy agreement.
kernels.firstGate: The experiment measures evidence accounting, not ideological convergence.

kernels.question: Does root-aware aggregation resist shared sensor or model failure?
kernels.null: It offers no robustness advantage over ordinary ensembles.
kernels.target: Lower confident error under common-mode failure with honest geographic coverage.
kernels.firstGate: Derived products sharing one instrument remain one dependency family.

kernels.question: Does root-aware sensor fusion reduce catastrophic decisions under correlated failure?
kernels.null: It does not outperform confidence-weighted fusion.
kernels.target: Lower catastrophic action rate without exceeding the preregistered fallback ceiling.
kernels.firstGate: Simulation and shadow mode only; no live actuation authority.

kernels.question: Does manuscript-family collapse improve alignment with expert genealogies and later discoveries?
kernels.null: Textual ancestry does not improve held-out adjudication.
kernels.target: Better family reconstruction and calibrated claim strength while preserving disputes.
kernels.primaryEndpoint: agreement with held-out expert source families
kernels.firstGate: The output preserves competing interpretations and missing archives.

kernels.question: Can a conclusion cross independent systems without losing roots, coverage, uncertainty, or authorization boundaries?
kernels.null: At least one independent implementation changes or drops a protected field.
kernels.target: Byte-verifiable semantic equivalence across two independent implementations and five processing stages.
kernels.firstGate: This alone may be named the first knowledge transaction; transaction-zero may not.
